nodes.prompt:
TASK: Dispatch exactly ONE bounded ChatGPT Web helper batch (two READ-ONLY parity-audit workers) for /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite and capture its authoritative terminal result.
PREP: The batch manifest already exists at /tmp/orca-parity-audit/manifest.json (labels: orca-parity-frontend, orca-parity-backend; workspace /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite). Read it first.
DISPATCH (single invocation, no other helper processes):
  mkdir -p /tmp/orca-parity-audit/reports
  jq -c /tmp/orca-parity-audit/manifest.json | /Users/indo/code/project/omo-bridge/target/release/delegate_to_chatgpt_web --batch-stdin --json
Run it as a background session and rely on the native completion notification (no polling loops, no duplicate watcher processes). Take ONE early peek at the session output to catch an immediate hard-reject (ok:false / invalid_arguments / rate-limit); if hard-rejected, report the verbatim error and stop.
Do NOT pass --browser-driver (browser driver discovery is cmux-first with Orca fallback). Do NOT pass --close-on-terminal (IDLE_RETAINED default). Do NOT resume or close any pre-existing scope. Do not spawn a second helper process for any reason, including retries.
DELIVERABLE:
1. The helper's complete terminal stdout saved verbatim to /tmp/orca-parity-audit/helper-output.json.
2. Each worker's final audit report extracted into /tmp/orca-parity-audit/reports/<label>.md (the terminal JSON's actual shape decides where the final message lives; if reports are richer in ~/.omo/bridge/task-state/*.json for the new scopes, copy the final notes there and say so).
3. Final message: per worker - label, scope_id, terminal_state, session_state, and a 5-line digest of its findings; plus where the full reports live.
SCOPE: You own only /tmp/orca-parity-audit/**. Read the manifest and helper output; never edit repository files; never touch browser tabs or scope files outside the helper contract.
VERIFY: The helper exits 0 and every worker reached ready=true before actual dispatch (visible in early output or ~/.omo/bridge/delegation-lifecycle/); the terminal JSON parses as JSON.
STOP WHEN: The helper's terminal JSON is saved and both worker reports are extracted, or the helper returns an authoritative terminal error (report it verbatim and stop - do not retry).

nodes.prompt:
TASK: Fan-in parity verdict for orca-lite: reconcile all evidence and decide, per axis, whether ui/ux/features (shortcuts, performance, settings page, ...) match the original Orca EXCLUDING by-design gaps, and whether the tree conforms to the design plan.
INPUTS (read all):
- /tmp/orca-parity-audit/local-gates.txt (command gates: cargo test, clippy, bun test, bun build)
- /tmp/orca-parity-audit/helper-output.json and /tmp/orca-parity-audit/reports/*.md (two web audit reports)
- /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite/ORCA_LITE_FIX_PLAN.md (design plan + release acceptance checklist)
- /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite/.omo/drafts/orca-ui-recovery.md (by-design scope boundary = gap list)
- The repo working tree (read-only) at /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite
BY-DESIGN GAP LIST (absence is not a defect): browser pane; editor/Monaco; PR views; remote-host management; automation; true agent-orchestration features; anything requiring Rust IPC absent from src-tauri/src/ipc/* (only worktree + terminal capabilities exist).
RE-CHECK these prior verification failures against the CURRENT tree (they failed before the uncommitted fixes; verify whether each is now resolved):
1. src-tauri/tests/worktree_safety.rs failed compile: PtyManager::spawn_in_worktree missing.
2. e2e_agent_workflow panicked unwrapping UnmergedBranch.
3. clippy -D warnings: WriterLeaseGuard never constructed / acquire_writer_lease unused.
4. ui/src/lib/ipcErrors.test.ts imported a then-nonexistent ./ipcErrors module.
5. createWorktree wrapper did not send the path field Rust's CreateWorktreeRequest requires - compare ui/src/lib/tauri.ts createWorktree with src-tauri/src/ipc/worktree.rs CreateWorktreeRequest field-by-field TODAY.
SPOT-CHECK: from each web audit report, re-verify at least 5 load-bearing citations (open the cited file:line, confirm the content supports the claimed status). A citation that fails re-verification flips that row to "unverified claim" and is listed separately. Also re-run ONE fast gate yourself as a sample re-check: bun run --cwd ui test from the repo root (record exit code).
DELIVERABLE (final message): a verdict table with columns axis | verdict(parity | by-design gap | defect | plan-deviation | unverified) | evidence; a per-prior-failure PASS/FAIL list; an overall verdict paragraph in Korean; an explicit list of defects requiring action, each with file:line.
SCOPE: READ-ONLY everywhere; you write nothing to disk.
VERIFY: every table row carries a citation you personally re-opened or a gate output you read from the captured artifacts.
STOP WHEN: verdict table + prior-failure list + overall paragraph are complete.
